- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 74–76 range), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect, failing to capture mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Model underestimates true outcomes when recent history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 70–72 range followed by 65–68).
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often underestimates the depth of a fall until 2–3 days later.
- When true outcome is below 70, model frequently forecasts 70–72, missing the downward trend.
- Model tends to overforecast in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, especially when true outcome is rising or near 70–72.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonal or cyclical patterns — e.g., consistently underestimates 68–70 range after 70+ peaks.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values when recent history is volatile — overconfident in upward momentum.
